concepts.name: Reading a radar chart
concepts.description: Each spoke is a category; how far a point sits from the centre is its value.

concepts.name: Bars and a line together
concepts.description: Two measures over the same years on one axis: compare them year by year.

concepts.name: Tables with missing values
concepts.description: Recover the blanks from row and column totals before answering.

concepts.name: Multi-step questions
concepts.description: Turn percentages into amounts, then apply a change: two or three steps in a row.

formulas.title: Reading a radar chart
formulas.prompt: How do you read a value off a radar chart?
formulas.formula:
One spoke per category
Value = distance from the centre (read the printed number)
Gap between two shapes on a spoke = difference
formulas.explanation: A radar chart is a bar chart wrapped round a circle: each spoke is a bar.
formulas.example: Asha 90 and Ravi 60 on the History spoke: a gap of 30.
formulas.commonMistake: Reading a value from the neighbouring spoke.
formulas.applicationPrompt: On which spoke are the two shapes furthest apart?

formulas.title: Bars and a line on one chart
formulas.prompt: A chart shows production as bars and sales as a line. What does the gap between them mean?
formulas.formula:
Same axis: bar − line = the difference for that year
Line above the bar → the second measure exceeds the first
formulas.explanation: Both measures use the same scale, so their difference is read straight off.
formulas.example: Production 70, sales 72: sales exceeded production by 2 that year.
formulas.commonMistake: Treating the line as a separate scale.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In which year does the line rise above the bar?

formulas.title: Filling a missing value
formulas.prompt: A table has blanks but its totals are complete. How do you fill a blank?
formulas.formula:
Missing = row total − the known parts
(or column total − the known parts)
formulas.explanation: Every row and column must add up, so one unknown in a line is fixed by the others.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding a column that still has a "?" in it.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Find the missing girls when the class total is 85 and boys are 45.

formulas.title: Percentages into amounts, then the change
formulas.prompt: A pie gives shares of an income. How do you answer "if X rises by p%, what happens to Y"?
formulas.formula:
Amount = Total × share%
Extra = Amount × p%
New Y = old Y − extra (if Y pays for it)
formulas.explanation: Work in rupees, not percentages, once the change starts.
formulas.example: ₹60,000 income, rent 25% = ₹15,000; a 20% rise adds ₹3,000, so savings of ₹12,000 fall to ₹9,000.
formulas.commonMistake: Taking p% of the whole income instead of the item.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Food is 30% of ₹50,000. It rises by 10%. How much more is spent?

formulas.title: Scan for the extreme first
formulas.prompt: A question asks which category is highest, lowest or most different. What do you do before calculating?
formulas.formula:
Look at the picture first: the furthest point, the tallest bar,
the widest gap. Then check only the two or three candidates.
formulas.explanation: Most "which is largest" questions are decided by eye; arithmetic is only needed to separate close candidates.
formulas.example: Five subjects: the widest gap is visibly History; confirm 90 − 60 = 30 against the next widest.
formulas.commonMistake: Calculating every value when two are clearly in the lead.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Which year shows the largest gap between the bar and the line?

formulas.title: Ratios straight from shares
formulas.prompt: Two items are 30% and 20% of the same total. What is the ratio of their amounts?
formulas.formula:
Ratio of amounts = ratio of shares
(the total cancels)
formulas.explanation: Both amounts are the same total times their share.
formulas.example: Food 30% and education 15%: food is twice education, whatever the income.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Rent is 25% and transport 10%. What is rent : transport?

levels.title: Radar Charts, Combos and Missing Data
levels.description: The chart types bank mains papers add on top of the basics.

blocks.title: A radar chart is a bar chart in a circle
blocks.body: Each spoke is one category and the distance from the centre is the value. Two series make two shapes; where they are furthest apart is where the difference is largest.

blocks.title: Bars and a line on one axis
blocks.body: A combo chart shows two measures over the same years, often production as bars and sales as a line. They share one scale, so the gap between the bar and the line is the difference for that year.

blocks.title: Missing values
blocks.body: Missing = row total − the known parts
blocks.caption: Fill every blank before you add a column or compare rows.

blocks.body: Look before you calculate: the largest gap or the tallest bar is usually visible at once. Do arithmetic only to separate close candidates.

questions.question: What is Asha's total score across the five subjects?

chart.caption: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100
chart.ariaSummary: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100. Asha: Maths 80, Science 70, English 60, History 90, Geography 75. Ravi: Maths 65, Science 85, English 70, History 60, Geography 80.

hints.text: Asha is the first series in the legend.

commonMistakes: Mixing in one of Ravi's values.

questions.question: In which subject is the gap between Asha's and Ravi's scores the largest?

chart.caption: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100
chart.ariaSummary: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100. Asha: Maths 80, Science 70, English 60, History 90, Geography 75. Ravi: Maths 65, Science 85, English 70, History 60, Geography 80.

questions.explanation: Gaps: Maths 15, Science 15, English 10, History 30, Geography 5. History is the largest.
questions.method: Find the spoke where the two shapes are furthest apart.

hints.text: Look first, then check the printed numbers.

commonMistakes: Choosing Science, Ravi's best subject, rather than the biggest gap.

questions.question: In which year were sales higher than production?

chart.caption: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units
chart.ariaSummary: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units. Production: 2020 50, 2021 60, 2022 55, 2023 70, 2024 80. Sales: 2020 45, 2021 58, 2022 50, 2023 72, 2024 75.

questions.explanation: Only in 2023 does the line (sales 72) sit above the bar (production 70).
solutionSteps: Compare the line with the bar each year.
questions.method: The line above the bar means sales exceeded production.

hints.text: Look for the year where the line rises above the top of the bar.

commonMistakes: Choosing 2024, the year with the highest sales.

questions.question: How many girls are there in class IX?

table.caption: Students in a school (some values missing)

questions.method: Missing value = row total − the known part.

hints.text: Use the total for class IX.

questions.question: In how many subjects did Ravi score more than Asha?

chart.caption: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100
chart.ariaSummary: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100. Asha: Maths 80, Science 70, English 60, History 90, Geography 75. Ravi: Maths 65, Science 85, English 70, History 60, Geography 80.

questions.explanation: Ravi is ahead in Science (85 > 70), English (70 > 60) and Geography (80 > 75): 3 subjects.
questions.method: Count the spokes where Ravi's point is further out.

hints.text: Go round the chart one spoke at a time.

commonMistakes: Counting a tie as a win.

questions.question: Over the five years, how many units (in thousands) were produced but not sold? (A year in which sales exceeded production counts as negative.)

chart.caption: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units
chart.ariaSummary: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units. Production: 2020 50, 2021 60, 2022 55, 2023 70, 2024 80. Sales: 2020 45, 2021 58, 2022 50, 2023 72, 2024 75.

questions.explanation: Production minus sales each year: 5 + 2 + 5 − 2 + 5 = 15 thousand.
questions.method: Subtract year by year, or subtract the two totals.
commonMistakes: Ignoring the year when sales were higher.

questions.question: What percentage of the 2022 production was sold? (to 2 decimal places)

chart.caption: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units
chart.ariaSummary: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units. Production: 2020 50, 2021 60, 2022 55, 2023 70, 2024 80. Sales: 2020 45, 2021 58, 2022 50, 2023 72, 2024 75.

hints.text: Divide the line's value by the bar's value.

questions.question: How many girls are there in the school altogether?

table.caption: Students in a school (some values missing)

questions.explanation: Fill the blanks first: VI 85 − 45 = 40 and IX 90 − 48 = 42. Then 40 + 38 + 45 + 42 + 44 = 209.
questions.method: Fill every blank in the column, then add.

questions.question: What is the ratio of boys to girls in class VII?

table.caption: Students in a school (some values missing)

questions.explanation: Boys in VII = 80 − 38 = 42, so boys : girls = 42 : 38 = 21 : 19.
questions.method: Fill the blank, then simplify the ratio.

hints.text: The boys' cell for VII is the blank.

commonMistakes: Writing the ratio the other way round.

questions.question: By how many marks does Asha's average per subject exceed Ravi's?

chart.caption: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100
chart.ariaSummary: Scores of Asha and Ravi out of 100. Asha: Maths 80, Science 70, English 60, History 90, Geography 75. Ravi: Maths 65, Science 85, English 70, History 60, Geography 80.

questions.method: Average = total ÷ 5 for each, then subtract.

hints.text: Difference of averages = difference of totals ÷ 5.

questions.question: Rent rises by 20% and the extra comes out of savings. How much will the family save each month?

chart.caption: Monthly budget of ₹60,000
chart.ariaSummary: Monthly budget of ₹60,000. Food 30%, Rent 25%, Education 15%, Transport 10%, Savings 20%.

questions.method: Percentages into rupees, then the change.

hints.text: Work out rent and savings in rupees first.

commonMistakes: Taking 20% of the income (₹12,000) as the extra.

questions.question: By what percentage did sales grow from 2020 to 2024? (to 2 decimal places)

chart.caption: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units
chart.ariaSummary: Production (bars) and sales (line) of a factory, thousand units. Production: 2020 50, 2021 60, 2022 55, 2023 70, 2024 80. Sales: 2020 45, 2021 58, 2022 50, 2023 72, 2024 75.

hints.text: Use the line, not the bars.

questions.question: Which class has the highest proportion of girls?

table.caption: Students in a school (some values missing)

solutionSteps: Compute girls ÷ total for each class.
questions.method: Fill the blanks, then compare girls ÷ total.

hints.text: Only class X has more girls than boys.

commonMistakes: Choosing VIII because it has the most girls (45), ignoring its larger total.
